title: Temperature-dependent risk of postoperative bleeding and pain perception following tonsillectomy
summary:
Tonsillectomy can lead to serious complications, particularly severe pain and postoperative bleeding. Previous studies indicate that ambient temperature can influence both the likelihood of postoperative bleeding and the level of pain experienced after surgery. However, the literature does not provide a clear consensus on the nature of this influence. We therefore aim to gather more data on this subject to improve the care of future tonsillectomy patients and potentially even prevent postoperative bleeding.
During the hospital stay following a tonsillectomy, the temperature and humidity in the patient's room will be measured daily. Patients will also be asked about their pain levels each day, rating them on a scale from 0 (no pain) to 10 (worst possible pain). During daily medical rounds, we will examine the surgical sites for signs of bleeding or inflammation. This will allow us to systematically collect data on the relationship between temperature and postoperative pain and bleeding.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All adult patients undergoing a tonsillectomy or abscess tonsillectomy at the ENT Clinic of Johannes Wesling Hospital Minden within a calendar year are to be included.
Exclusion criteria:
Exclusion criteria include: an inability to communicate in German that limits the assessment of the pain scale; a pre-existing blood coagulation disorder (including that resulting from the perioperative use of oral anticoagulants such as Xarelto, Apixaban, or Marcumar); advanced hepatic insufficiency; a Quick value below 60%; and patients treated as inpatients at the facility for post-tonsillectomy hemorrhage following surgery performed elsewhere. The study population comprises patients aged 18 years and older.
